Subject: Cognify onboarding — model shortlist and sizing

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking us on. Quick background: Cognify is rolling out an automated summarization and compliance-extraction feature for our customer support workflows. We expect the feature to be live for a pilot in Q1. Key asks for onboarding:

- Model shortlist recommendation for accuracy-latency tradeoffs
- Context window guidance (chat history + 2-3 docs per ticket)
- Token volume estimate for first 90 days (we have historical ticket volumes)

I've attached a CSV with sample ticket lengths and a short product spec. Our initial pilot will cover ~12k MAUs (support users), ~3% conversion to summary per day (~360 summaries/day), but agents will run multi-step prompts so expected completions per summary ~1.6 on avg. Latency target is <400ms p95.

Attachments: cognify_token_profile_q4.csv, product_spec.md

Can we sync this week for a 30-min tech handoff? Prefer Wed or Thu morning PST.

Best,
Lily

Thanks Lily — happy to run the handoff. Wed 12/6 09:00 PST or Thu 12/7 10:00 PST both work for a 30-min sync; I'll book the earlier if I don't hear back.

Quick checklist before the call so we can have a productive sizing discussion:
- Confirm sample CSV (you attached) includes representative ticket length and tokens per field
- Clarify the number of docs we need to keep in context (you mentioned 2-3) — are those full attachments, extracted snippets, or both?
- Expected concurrency during pilot peak hours (est. concurrent agents or API requests)
- Any regulatory/PII constraints for caching or retention

Preliminary reading: with the numbers you gave, we'll look at three model classes: small-low-latency (<4B), mid (7B-13B) for balanced cost/quality, and long-context (>30B/long-window) for tickets with multi-document context. Also will prepare token-volume buckets (daily/weekly/90d) and an ops plan for canary traffic and fallback routing.

I'll loop Ben (model infra) and Grace (CS ops) into the call so we can cover runtime trade-offs and rollout mechanics.

Thanks — see you on the call.

—Tessa

Thanks Tessa. Wed 12/6 09:00 PST confirmed. Attaching the token profile CSV you asked for (sample includes ticket body, subject, and up to 2 attachments when present). A quick data summary below: 

- Historical active users (MAU): 12,000
- Daily tickets: 12,000 tickets/day (roughly 1 ticket/user/day during peak)
- Pilot scope: 3% of traffic -> 360 tickets/day processed by the feature
- Avg ticket length (body + subject): 600 tokens (median 420, 95p 1,800)
- Attachments: present in ~8% of tickets; when present we extract a 400-token snippet on avg
- Expected completions per request: 1.6 (1.0 summary + follow-up clarifications)
- Peak concurrency window: 10:00-14:00 PST, ~40 requests/minute to the feature in pilot (estimated)

Security: all PII must be redacted before long-term storage; short-lived KV caching within VPC is allowed.

Attachments: cognify_token_profile_q4.csv

See you Wed.

—Lily
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, Lily Tran <lily.tran@cognify.ai>

Subject: Re: Cognify onboarding — preliminary sizing notes

Hi all — did a quick pass on the numbers Lily shared and sketched out expected token volumes and model tradeoffs. Notes below, will present these at the Wed call and follow up with a short spreadsheet.

Summary of calculations (pilot = 360 tickets/day):
- Input tokens per request: avg 600 (ticket) + 400 attachment snippet * 8% present ≈ 632 tokens
- Prompt tokens (including system + instructions): ~120 tokens per request
- Completion tokens: avg 240 tokens per completion; with 1.6 completions => 384 tokens
- Total tokens per request = 632 + 120 + 384 = 1,136 tokens
- Daily token volume (pilot): 360 * 1,136 ≈ 409,000 tokens/day
- 90-day estimate: ~36.8M tokens (includes 15% buffer for retries and spikes)

Concurrency and throughput:
- Peak RPS estimate: 40 requests/min ≈ 0.67 rps during peak; with 1.6 completions and avg generation time these translate to burst capacity needs for short windows; latency p95 target <400ms will favor smaller models with aggressive batching disabled for low-latency paths or LRU prefix caching.

Context length guidance:
- Baseline: 2,048 tokens covers typical ticket + instructions
- For multi-doc + longer histories: 8,192 tokens recommended as an option (we can route these to long-window model variants)

Model shortlist (tradeoffs):
- rwd-lowlat-3b (quantized): best p50/p95 latency, lowest cost, acceptable for extractive summaries but lower factuality on very long contexts
- rwd-balanced-13b: sweet spot for quality vs cost; good for mixed summarization + compliance extraction
- rwd-long-70b (large long-window): required if you need to include full attachments + 30-day thread history in context; higher cost and slower but preserves context fidelity

Operational recommendations:
- Canary with 10% of pilot traffic on rwd-balanced-13b, fallback to rwd-lowlat-3b on capacity or timeouts
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated templates (e.g., similar agent prompts) to reduce token counts by up to ~20%
- Quantize rwd-balanced-13b for Dedicated if customer opts for lower unit cost; preserve one non-quantized variant for evals

I'll attach the quick spreadsheet after the call with token buckets and cost projections (expected hosted cost approx $X/day for pilot — we'll refine on the call).

Best,
Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Cognify onboarding — rollout and runbook items

Thanks Ben — that looks good. A few ops items for the onboarding runbook I want to track before pilot kickoff:

- Canary plan: 10% traffic for 2 weeks, health checks include latency, error rate, and summary quality sample (we'll run a daily eval set)
- Alerting thresholds: p95 latency > 600ms, error rate > 1%
- Fallback policy: route to rwd-lowlat-3b with a short banner to agents if a fallback is used more than 5x/hour
- Data retention: ingest only redacted outputs to analytics S3; raw inputs deleted after 24h unless doc retention requested by Cognify legal
- PO/invoicing cadence: pilot billed monthly, pre-approved credit limit of $5k for the pilot phase

Next steps for this thread: Ben to post the cost spreadsheet, Tessa to share the onboarding checklist link, Lily to confirm PO and compliance sign-off. I've also linked a starter runbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1AbCdEfG-handoff-plan

—Grace
